Michael Carrick is set to remain in charge of Manchester United for this weekend’s Premier League match away to Chelsea, according to media reports on Tuesday. Carrick’s future at Old Trafford has been the subject of intense speculation after a miserable run of eight games without a win. Sunday’s 3-0 humbling at home to Bournemouth left the English giants just one point above the Premier League relegation zone. But the BBC, Sky Sports and Britain’s Press Association all reported that the former United and England midfielder would take the team to Stamford Bridge on Saturday. Carrick arrived at United’s Carrington training ground on Tuesday to oversee a routine training session. Make PUNCH part of your everyday experience. Add us to your Preferred Sources The BBC cited “sources” as saying the 45-year-old would be given a chance by the United hierarchy to turn things around. Carrick was handed a two-year deal in May after overseeing an impressive revival as caretaker boss following United’s struggles under Ruben Amorim. The club recovered to finish third in the Premier League, earning a return to the Champions League. Ajayi hails Hull’s response against Brentford EPL: I’m not expecting to be sacked, says Carrick Manchester United suffer eighth winless match against Bournemouth But United have won just two of 12 matches in all competitions so far this season, with a return of seven points from eight league games representing their worst start to a league season in 40 years. Carrick avoided directly answering questions about his future following the Bournemouth loss. The United boss acknowledged the crowd at full-time as fans chanted his name in a show of support for the beleaguered manager, but they vented their anger at the players and club hierarchy. United great Wayne Rooney, who played alongside Carrick at Old Trafford, aimed at the players following a string of poor performances. “The players haven’t got a leg to stand on. What’s not fair is the performances they are giving,” he told the Stick to United podcast. “I looked at the fans; you could see the pain and anger in their faces when those players are walking around the football pitch.” AFP Kindly share this story:
